fields.name: Gadādhara (disciple of Śyāmānanda)
fields.notes:
He was a disciple of Śyāmānanda Prabhu, of the Śrīpāṭa of Gopīballabhpur (Prema-vilāsa 20).

The record also held the Gadādhara of Barahanpura who installed Lālavihārī, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
A devotee from Barahanpura who installed the Deity of Lālavihārī (Bhaktamālā 25.3). Taken out of the record «Gadādhara» #275, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was a disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.133).

The record also held the Gopāla Ācārya of the Narottama-vilāsa and the Gopāla Ācārya of Lord Caitanya's branch, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
His name is recorded in the Narottama-vilāsa. Taken out of the record «Gopāla Ācārya» #345, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).
He belonged to the branch of Lord Caitanya (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.114; Nāmāmṛta-samudra 135). Taken out of the record «Gopāla Ācārya» #345, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

The sixth descendant in the family of Rāja Vīra Hāmvīra of Viṣṇupura; he ruled the state from 1712 to 1748 A.D. and composed a kāvya on Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-līlā.

The record also held Gopīnātha Siṁha of Lord Caitanya's branch («Akrūra»), now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He belonged to the branch of Lord Caitanya, who called him «Akrūra» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.76). Taken out of the record «Gopāla Siṁha» #362, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Gopījanavallabha (son-in-law of Śrīnivāsa)
fields.notes:
The son-in-law and disciple of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya. His father was Rāmakṛṣṇa Caṭṭarāja and his Śrīpāṭa was at Budhuipāḍā in Murshidabad; he married Hemalatā Devī, Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's eldest daughter (Karṇānanda 1).

The record also held Gopījanavallabha the eldest son of Vīracandra, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
The eldest son of Vīracandra Prabhu (Prema-vilāsa 24). Taken out of the record «Gopijanavallabha» #372, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Gopīkṛṣṇa Dāsa (disciple of Śyāmānandī Dāmodara)
fields.notes:
He was a disciple of Śyāmānandī Dāmodara.

The record also held Gopīkṛṣṇa Dāsa the author of the Harināma-kavaca, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He was the author of the book Harināma-kavaca. Taken out of the record «GOPĪKṚṢṆA Dāsa» #378, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Gopīnātha Brahmacārī (associate of Vṛndāvana dāsa)
fields.notes:
An intimate associate of Vṛndāvana dāsa, the author of the Caitanya-bhāgavata. He was the son of Gopāla, the youngest son of Balabhadra, and the first of the brahmacārī clan of Denuḍa village in Burdwan.

The record also held the Gopīnātha disciple of Rasikānanda and the Gopīnātha disciple of Śyāmānanda, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Dakṣiṇa 4.19). Taken out of the record «Gopīnātha» #389, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple of Śyāmānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Pūrva 1.32). Taken out of the record «Gopīnātha» #389, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was a disciple of Narottama Ṭhākura (Prema-vilāsa 20, Narottama-vilāsa 12).

The record also held the Govinda Rāya of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's family, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He descended from the family of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya (Anurāga-vallī 7). Taken out of the record «Govinda Rāya» #419, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

The father of the well-known Bengali poet Rajanikanta Sen. Guruprasāda compiled a padāvalī collection, the Pada-cintāmaṇi-mālā, most of its padas in Vrajabuli; first published in 1283 (1876 A.D.), with his introduction on the sounds and grammar of Vrajabuli.

fields.name: Hari (disciple of Rasikānanda)
fields.notes:
He was a disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.111).

The record also held the Sanskrit poet Hari of the Padyāvalī, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
A Sanskrit poet whose name is in the Padyāvalī (Viśvakoṣa vol. 22, p. 479). Taken out of the record «Hari» #460, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was the teacher of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Pūrva 9.49).

The record also said «the son of Mādhava Miśra, also named Vāṇīnātha» (Prema-vilāsa 20): that is Vāṇīnātha Paṇḍita, Gadādhara's brother (#1641), not this Jagannātha; nor Lord Caitanya's father, «Jagannātha Miśra (Purandara)».

fields.name: Jayarāma Cakravartī
fields.notes:
A disciple of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya; his Śrīpāṭa was at Kausona in Gauḍa (Anurāga-vallī 7). Śyāma Bhaṭṭa, Kṛṣṇa Purohita and Jayarāma lived in the same village (Karṇānanda 1).

The record also held the Jayarāma of Navadvīpa, maternal grandfather of Svarūpa Dāmodara, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).

A resident of Navadvīpa, the maternal grandfather of Svarūpa Dāmodara; Padmagarbhācārya married his daughter (Prema-vilāsa 24). Taken out of the record «Jayarama Cakravartī» #607, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Jayarāma (commentator of the Padyāmṛta-taraṅgiṇī)
fields.notes:
He wrote a ṭīkā of the Padyāmṛta-taraṅgiṇī entitled Sapanaracana (Viśvakoṣa vol. VI, p. 682).

The record also held the Vedāntist Jayarāmācārya, author of the Pāṣaṇḍa-capeṭikā, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).

A Vedāntist, also known as Jayarāmācārya and Vijayarāmācārya. He wrote in Sanskrit the Pāṣaṇḍa-capeṭikā, with arguments against the philosophy of the Madhva-sampradāya (Viśvakoṣa vol. VI, p. 682). Taken out of the record «Jayarama» #612, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Kamalākānta Dāsa (disciple of Jagadīśa Paṇḍita)
fields.notes:
A resident of Durgāpur and a disciple of Jagadīśa Paṇḍita (Caitanya-maṅgala of Jayānanda 12.4).

The record also held Kamalākānta Dāsa the Vrajabuli poet of the Padaratnākara, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).

Famous for his verses in Vrajabuli; twelve or thirteen of his padas are in the Padaratnākara, which he published in 1806. Taken out of the record «Kamalākānta Dāsa» #648, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Kamalākara Dāsa Ṭhākura
fields.notes:
His title was Ṭhākura, and he was probably a brāhmaṇa. In the Vaiṣṇava-vandanā his name comes next to Kamalākara Pippalāi. According to the Pāṭa-paryaṭana he was a disciple of Abhirāma Gosvāmī.

The record also held Kamalākara Dāsa the father of Locana dāsa, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
A vaidya, the father of Locana dāsa, the author of the Caitanya-maṅgala (see «Locana dāsa»). Taken out of the record «Kamalakara Dāsa» #656, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).
